subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: How does the reactivity of the Group 7 halogens change going down the group?
questions.explain: Halogen reactivity decreases down Group 7 as gaining an electron becomes harder.

questions.q: Why is aluminium extracted by electrolysis rather than reduction with carbon?
options: Aluminium is more reactive than carbon
Aluminium does not form an ore
Aluminium is less reactive than carbon
questions.explain: Aluminium is more reactive than carbon, so carbon cannot reduce its oxide and electrolysis must be used.

questions.q: When silver nitrate solution is added to a chloride solution, the precipitate formed is:
questions.explain: Chloride ions form a white precipitate of silver chloride with silver nitrate.

questions.q: Compared with Group 1 metals, transition metals are generally:
questions.explain: Transition metals are typically harder, stronger, denser and less reactive than Group 1 metals.

questions.q: How does the reactivity of the Group 1 alkali metals change going down the group?
questions.explain: Reactivity increases down Group 1 as the outer electron is more easily lost.

questions.q: Flame emission spectroscopy works by measuring the:
options: Light given out when metal ions are heated in a flame
questions.explain: In flame emission spectroscopy, heated metal ions emit light with a pattern that identifies them.

questions.q: Where are non-metals generally found in the periodic table?
questions.explain: Non-metals are located on the right-hand side of the periodic table.

questions.q: How does the boiling point of the noble gases change going down Group 0?
questions.explain: Boiling points increase down Group 0 as the atoms get larger.

questions.q: Which halogen is the most reactive?
questions.explain: Fluorine, at the top of Group 7, is the most reactive halogen.

questions.q: The modern periodic table arranges elements in order of increasing:
questions.explain: Elements are ordered by increasing atomic number (number of protons).

questions.q: Mendeleev left gaps in his periodic table because he:
options: Predicted elements that were not yet discovered
Could not order the known elements
Wanted to separate metals from non-metals
questions.explain: Mendeleev left gaps for undiscovered elements and predicted their properties.

questions.q: Bronze is an alloy mainly of copper and which other element?
questions.explain: Bronze is an alloy of copper and tin.

questions.q: Which of these is a property typical of Group 1 metals?
questions.explain: Alkali metals are soft enough to cut with a knife and have low densities.

questions.q: Oxygen gas can be identified because it:
questions.explain: Oxygen relights a glowing splint.

questions.q: A period in the periodic table is a:
questions.explain: A period is a horizontal row; elements across a period gain electrons in the same shell.

questions.q: In which group are the alkali metals found?
questions.explain: The alkali metals are the elements of Group 1.

questions.q: The halogens exist as molecules made of:
questions.explain: Halogens are diatomic, e.g. Cl2, Br2 and I2.

questions.q: Why are the Group 0 noble gases unreactive?
options: They have a full outer shell of electrons
questions.explain: Noble gases have full (stable) outer electron shells, so they rarely react.

questions.q: Why is the reactivity of Group 1 metals greater further down the group?
options: The outer electron is further from the nucleus and more easily lost
They have more protons in the outer shell
The outer electron is closer to the nucleus
questions.explain: The outer electron is further from the nucleus and less strongly attracted, so it is lost more easily.

questions.q: Which property is typical of transition metals but not Group 1 metals?
options: They are solids at room temperature
questions.explain: Transition metals commonly form coloured compounds and act as catalysts.

questions.q: Which element is in Group 7 and Period 3 of the periodic table?
questions.explain: Chlorine is in Group 7 (halogens) and Period 3.

questions.q: Lithium reacts with water. Which observation is correct?
options: It fizzes and floats, releasing hydrogen
questions.explain: Lithium floats and fizzes on water, giving off hydrogen and forming lithium hydroxide.

specSource: OCR GCSE (9–1) Chemistry (Gateway A) (J248) specification; Predicting Identifying Reactions
